messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Chromosome explorer - zooms 64 + 128.
parts:
Hi,

especially those zoom levels generate very large PNGs. They might be
too large for your PNG device driver. Depending on your system, there
are few different PNG drivers available to R. You can override the
one that aroma.affymetrix uses, but overriding the findPngDevice()
function.

Search the group page for "override findPngDevice()" and you should
get some threads with suggestions and success stories for this.

Note also that Firefox will have problem displaying the greater zoom
levels for some of the larger chromosomes.

Hope this helps

/Henrik

messages.author: 8ae1efaa2cf53fab
messages.subject: Re: Chromosome explorer - zooms 64 + 128.
parts:
Hi all,

I've re-installed all packages.
The .pngs that are being created are still very small and do not
display - the files are not corrupt as such, I can open the pngs,
however they are empty of content. They are only 13k in size,
compared to 422k for the viewable pngs (I am only looking at zooms 64
+ 128).
The pngs that are failing are only those for the larger chromosomes -
anything from chr7 onwards is being successfully generated.
The only error that I can detect is, upon loading EBImage:

Warning messages:
1: In dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) :
failed to initialize GTK+. GTK+ dependent functions will not work

From the EBImage/aroma.affymetrix documentation, I am not certain that
this is the cause of the problem.
I am not receiving any errors regarding any memory issues.

Can anyone suggest any tests that I can run to help pinpoint the
problem?
For example, what is the last file generated that is passed to the
command to create the .png? Is it the .xdr file?, in which case, that
does not look like the problem - all of these files are generated
successfully, with chr02 files being the largest at ~3.4Mb, and chr24
at 203k.

Any assistance greatly appreciated.

with regards

Lavinia Gordon.

Mark (or others),

I have similar problems (Mac OS X 10.5.6 Servert, latest R, latest
A.a; had them with older versions, too).

Generally, there also could be an alternative solution for generating
the plots, as long as it produces similar output (single values +
segments). I have written my own web scripts for visualization &
GoldenPath linking, but they use the CE plots for detail
representation (I can provide anyone interested with a link).

Michael.
